title: Which halls paid tips: Hunts and Nagel's, Mama Lou's, West End
summary: Dawson says he made tips only at Hunts and Nagel's, Harry Parker's and the lakefront places with small bands; heavy-band dances were fixed price.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I tried to get Pete to play, you know, the Entertainer and different Red Back numbers, from out of that book, and he wouldn't play them at Preservation. He was playing all this time. And everybody didn't understand why. But he didn't think he should play them at Preservation. Well, let's see what we got next. Uh, what were some of the best halls that you ever played in? I mean, for making good tips. You played in big halls here?

I never made no tips though. Only, only halls I made tips was, uh, was, uh, Hanson Nagel, and the Rays in Ivorville, Harry Parker, uh, Saratoga, uh, Saratoga and, uh, Ivorville. Billy Phillips was on, uh, Saratoga near the next corner of, uh, uh, uh, uh, more near Benville.

What about, did you ever go to Dixieland, ever play at Dixieland Hall in late years? No? You never played there? I thought maybe you'd make some tips. You know, I'm talking about where Cottrell and Papa French money, you never made tips there. No. No.

Well, it's funny. I would think that, you know, you'd make some good money at Jean Zami or Frantz Zami, but the band didn't get the tips? No, no, we, uh, we had a study, uh, uh, uh, stipulated price, you know. You're regular sound. They had a fixed, they had a fixed price, and the leader would charge them so much for the band. Uh-huh. And that's all. When we had so many hours to play, and that's all. When we start the playing, when it's time to knock off, we knock off, and they pay us off. No tips. There are people that tip you there. Yeah. What about the lakefront? Oh, now, lakefront. Now, Mama Lou, and, uh, the Happy Landing, them's the places where I was going to go. There are tons of places where I made tips there. Yeah. West End? Did you ever play out at West End? Yeah. Played at West End. Spanish Port and Millenburg. All the places. Yeah. I played out there with Tom Brown and them, and I'll tell you, this was Walter Preston and them. And you got tips there. Yeah, yeah. Short band. See, four pieces. What about Millenburg? Did you get tips there? Millenburg? No, I didn't make no tips. Every time I played Millenburg, I played with a heavy band, you know. And they just played for a straight,
Right, yeah, salary. That's all. Is Millenburg and Spanish Port and the West End changed much? Oh, yeah.
